blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can bill an order several times) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Charge call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts with exponential backoff), retry only errors where the charge certainly did not happen (connection refused, 429, 503) and send an idempotency key derived from the order id so the provider deduplicates a repeated POST; after the last attempt, raise an error naming the order. Scenario: the provider accepts the charge but the response is lost (read error) or a 5xx comes back after processing — the loop POSTs again every second and the customer is charged twice or more; when the provider is down or rejects the request permanently (400, 401, 402), checkout spins forever at one request per second against the provider.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can bill an order several times

findings.recommendation: Pass `timeout=(connect, read)` to `requests.post`, e.g. `timeout=(3, 10)`. Scenario: the provider accepts the TCP connection but never answers — `requests` waits indefinitely, the checkout worker is stuck with no error and no log, and an operator sees only hung requests. Note that a read timeout on a POST is ambiguous (the charge may have happened), so it must only be retried with the idempotency key of R-ops-1.
findings.title: Charge call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields — order_id, attempt, HTTP status, provider error code, exception type — never the request body or credentials, and log the final failure at error level. Scenario: the provider returns 402 or 500 for an order — nothing is logged, so an operator at 3 a.m. cannot tell which order is failing, why, or that the provider is failing at all.
findings.title: Charge failures are swallowed with no log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL (and its credentials, when added) from the environment or the application's configuration, failing at start-up when it is missing. Scenario: tasks.md verifies the charge against the provider's sandbox, but the code always targets the production endpoint — a test or staging environment either charges real orders, or needs a code edit to point at the sandbox.
findings.title: Provider URL is hard-coded instead of read from configuration
